messages:
maria: Heads-up — CI is red for branch `feat/slim-base`. Build job completed but the image push step failed when publishing to our registry. I dug into the logs but wanted to flag here in case anyone sees something obvious. <https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/12345|ci/12345>

maria: error snippet from runner:
```
Step 24/27 : PUSH image to registry
---
failed to push to registry: failed to upload blob: server returned unexpected status: 403 Forbidden
Error: denied: requested access to the resource is denied
```

sam: ugh. did you change the image name/tag format in the Dockerfile or CI config?

maria: no, only swapped base image to `slim-alpine:3.18` and removed some apt cruft. CI tag format is the same (sha + short branch name).

ci-bot: Build #12345 — push step exited with code 1 (push-image). Logs archived: <https://ci.redwood.dev/artifacts/12345/push.log> :warning:

leo: can you try a manual push from the runner? sometimes buildkit caches a layer with stale metadata and registry rejects the manifest. quick test: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --push --no-cache -t registry.internal/redwood/xyz:tmp`

maria: tried on my laptop with `--no-cache` and got the same `denied` response. I also tried `docker login` against the registry and it succeeded (my token), so seems CI creds might be the issue?

sam: CI service account token was rotated yesterday for scoped keys, maybe the deploy role lost ecr:PutImage or equivalent. @jen can you check IAM / registry permissions?

jen: checking. I see yesterday a key rotation for `ci-deployer` at 09:12. The new key got loaded to the secrets manager, but the pipeline uses a different secret path. looks like the deploy job is still pulling the old secret (expired).

jen: repro locally by simulating expired creds: `docker push` -> `unauthorized: authentication required` vs the CI log shows `denied` which is consistent with a perms problem. I’ll update the secret and re-run the job.

maria: thanks. while you're at it can you also check the registry quota? sometimes we hit a rate-limit and see weird 403s.

jen: checked quota — fine. rotating secret now and kicking off rebuild.

ci-bot: Re-run requested by jen — queued build #12346.

maria: if this fails again, next steps: clear builder cache on the runner with `docker buildx prune --force --all` and try pushing to the staging registry (`staging-registry.internal/...`) to isolate whether it's permission vs artifact problem.

leo: another thought — our Dockerfile adds a tiny random metadata file for provenance (timestamp). That can cause different manifests but shouldn't reject push. still, worth removing nondeterminism if we keep hitting digest mismatches.

ci-bot: Build #12346 completed — push step failed again (same error). logs: <https://ci.redwood.dev/artifacts/12346/push.log>

sam: ok, now I'm thinking maybe CI runner builder instance has an old docker credential helper cached. can someone ssh into the runner and confirm `docker-credential-helpers` state?

jen: i tried an interactive job — confirmed the runner is using the secret from the old path despite the update. There's a second helper that pulls a cached secret from `/var/lib/ci/secret-cache`. I'll purge that and requeue.

maria: on it: I triggered a manual login in the interactive runner using `aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <account>.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` (we're on ECR). After that, a push from the runner succeeded for a test image.

maria: pushed `registry.internal/redwood/ci-sanity:manual-test` to confirm perms.

leo: nice — so root cause is stale secret cache on runners + earlier token rotation. We should add a pipeline step to force refresh credentials before push (or invalidate that cache on rotation).

jen: agreed. I'll put up a PR to the infra repo to add `aws ecr get-login-password | docker login ...` as a pre-push step and also add a rotation hook that clears `/var/lib/ci/secret-cache` on runners.

maria: PR LGTM once tests pass. assigning to jen for follow-up and scheduling a quick postmortem note. :white_check_mark:

sam: can we also add a retry for push step (exponential backoff x3)? transient auth flaps are annoying.

jen: will include a retry. thanks folks.

maria: resolution: manual login fixed push; infra PR to refresh secrets + cache invalidation + push retry. tagging for deployment and will watch next CI runs.

leo: thanks — leaving a short runbook: 1) check CI push logs, 2) `docker login` on runner, 3) `docker buildx prune` if suspect cache, 4) re-run job.

ci-bot: Thread closed by maria — follow-up PR: <https://git.redwood.dev/infra/merge_requests/789> :lock:
